audit_result.code_path: supabase/migrations/0000_create_member_schema.sql::policy:Allow user to update their own profile::L83
audit_result.proof_trace: The UPDATE policy for `member.members` (authenticated role) uses only `USING (auth.uid() = id)` with no `WITH CHECK` clause; PostgreSQL falls back to the USING expression as the write check, which is a row-identity guard only and places no constraint on `is_admin`, `status`, or `generation`. Default privileges grant `authenticated` full column-level write access (L16-18), and no subsequent migration adds a column-level REVOKE or corrective WITH CHECK — the security fix migration (20260317000001) adds FORCE RLS but does not patch the UPDATE policy.
audit_result.attack_scenario: An authenticated user sends `PATCH https://<project>.supabase.co/rest/v1/members?id=eq.<their-uuid>` with body `{"is_admin": true}` and their JWT; the RLS USING check passes, the fallback WITH CHECK passes, and the row is updated — granting full admin privileges system-wide including OAuth application management.

PROP-0000-create-inv-001.text: Members UPDATE RLS policy must include WITH CHECK restricting writable columns.
PROP-0000-create-inv-001.assertion: policy(members, authenticated, UPDATE).with_check != true AND restricts_columns(policy, [is_admin, status, generation])
